title: perf(canary): automated latency/throughput regression detection + rollout guards
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: we need automated, production-safe detection of performance regressions (latency and throughput) during canary rollouts and an automatic rollout guard that prevents bad variants from reaching production. This PR implements a continuous canary detector and rollout-guard controller that integrates with the rollout service and the perf-canary dashboard. Changes include a sliding-window baseline estimator per-route/model, EWMA-based sensitivity tuning, p90/p95/p99 regression detectors with configurable hysteresis, and automatic traffic rollback/traffic-shift hold when sustained regressions are detected. The detector is KV-cache aware (ignores cold-start spikes by annotating initial requests), supports per-customer thresholds, and emits structured events for the observability pipeline. Feature is behind a runtime feature-flag (perf_canary.autodetect) and defaults to off for non-Dedicated customers. Test plan: unit tests for detectors and controller, perf-smoke e2e against benchmark-lab images, staged rollout to canary fleet with synthetic load, and manual validation using perf-canary dashboard. Related: ENG-4123, ENG-4130. Checklist: [x] detector implementation, [x] rollout guard + controller, [x] docs and runbook, [x] e2e smoke tests, [x] perf benchmarks and CI gating. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps thresholds conservative (5-10% p95 tolerance) and provides an override API for SRE to adjust sensitivity per-release.
commits_summary: 3 commits: detector: implement sliding-window baseline and EWMA sensitivity; controller: integrate with rollout service and add rollback/hold actions; tests/docs: add e2e perf smoke tests and runbook.
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can the detector distinguish KV-cache cold-starts vs real regressions? Please add a flag to ignore first N requests per instance.
Maya Chen: Added cold-start exclusion with annotator; default N=50 but configurable per-route.
Lina Torres: Will these events flood PagerDuty? Can we aggregate alerts and only page on sustained regressions?
Maya Chen: Controller aggregates events and only escalates after hysteresis window; runbook updated with paging thresholds.
Ben Carlson: CI perf-smoke is flaky on r5 nodes, observed 10% variance; suggest increasing sample size.
Maya Chen: Increased sample windows in perf-smoke and added retry for CI stability.
release_notes: Add automated performance canary detector and rollout guards. New runtime flag perf_canary.autodetect=false by default. Operators can enable per-route detection and tune thresholds via the perf-canary dashboard or API. This helps detect sustained p95 latency regressions and throughput drops and will automatically hold or rollback canaries to protect production traffic.
summary_metrics: cold-start-ignore: first 50 requests per instance default
rationale: Automating detection reduces manual monitoring overhead and provides faster rollback for regressions while keeping conservative defaults to avoid false positives. Integration with rollout engine enables immediate protection without human-in-the-loop for clear regressions.
test_plan: Unit tests for detector math and controller logic; perf-smoke e2e run in CI; staged rollout to 5% canaries for 24h with synthetic load; manual verification via perf-canary dashboard; rollback exercised in staging.
notes: Feature gated, rollout scheduled with SRE for initial opt-in to Dedicated customers. Follow-up PR will add ML-based anomaly scoring and adaptive thresholds.
